title: Telemetry Normalization and Fidelity Acceptance Playbook for Enterprise Tenants
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the telemetry normalization, fidelity acceptance criteria, and handoff process for enterprise tenants onboarding to Redwood Inference. It ensures telemetry received from tenant environments maps cleanly into our observability pipeline (ingress-gateway -> telemetry-gatekeeper -> telemetry-pipeline -> metrics-aggregator), meets fidelity thresholds for QBR reporting, and contains cost attribution fields required for tenant-level billing.

Audience: Customer Success, Integrations Engineers, Observability/Monitoring, SRE, and the tenant technical contact.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable acceptance checklist for tenant telemetry during onboarding.
- Enforce minimum fidelity and completeness requirements so QBR metrics, cost attribution, and SLIs are trustworthy.
- Reduce back-and-forth during cutover by codifying normalization rules and validation queries.

Scope

Includes: metric names, label/tag normalization, span/trace expectations, required tenant metadata (tenant_id, environment, region, cost_center), retention and sampling guidance for dedicated/private tenants.
Excludes: application-level debugging not relevant to service-level SLOs (those are covered in the Tenant Debugging Playbook).

Key Definitions

- Fidelity: Percent of expected telemetry signals that are present and correctly formatted for a representative test traffic set.
- Normalization: The transformation rules applied to incoming metric names and labels so they align with Redwood canonical schema.
- Acceptance Window: The 72-hour validation period during which metrics are assessed against acceptance criteria before enabling compute-level billing and SLA reporting.

Acceptance Criteria (must all be met to mark telemetry as Accepted)

1) Ingestion and Latency
 - Metrics delivered to telemetry-pipeline ingestion topic within 60 seconds 95% of the time during the Acceptance Window.
 - Traces sampled at the agreed rate (default 1% for hosted, 5% for Dedicated during onboarding) with an end-to-end delivery latency < 120s for 99th percentile.

2) Metric Coverage & Fidelity
 - For the tenant's representative traffic replay (or production ramp), at least 98% of the expected metric families are observed (see required metric families table below).
 - Label fidelity: required labels (tenant_id, route_id, model_id, region, environment) must be present on >= 99% of tokens/requests metrics.

3) Naming & Normalization
 - Metric and label names conform to Redwood canonical names after normalization rules are applied (see Normalization Rules section).

4) Cost Attribution
 - cost_center and billing_tag labels populated on per-request or per-batch metrics, or alternate agreed mechanism validated via test traffic.

5) Data Retention & Access
 - Telemetry retention matches contract (default 90 days for enterprise onboarding window).
 - Observability roles for tenant contacts configured (read-only vs edit) and verified.

Required Metric Families (representative table)

| Category | Canonical metric name | Description | Min cardinality |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Ingress | redwood.ingress.requests | per-request ingress counter (labels: tenant_id, route_id) | high |
| Latency | redwood.request.latency_ms | request latency histogram (labels: tenant_id, model_id) | high |
| Tokens | redwood.tokens.generated | tokens generated per request | medium |
| Errors | redwood.request.errors | 4xx/5xx error counter (labels: tenant_id, code) | medium |
| VM/GPU Util | redwood.host.gpu.utilization | GPU utilization gauge for Dedicated hosts | low |

Normalization Rules (applied by telemetry-gatekeeper)

1) Metric name mapping: tenant metrics with prefixes are mapped to canonical names. Example mapping JSON (example shown inline):

  {
    "mappings": [
      {"source_prefix": "myapp.requests", "target": "redwood.ingress.requests"},
      {"source_prefix": "latency_ms", "target": "redwood.request.latency_ms"}
    ]
  }

2) Label canonicalization: alias labels are normalized (e.g., ns -> tenant_id, env -> environment). All tenant-generated labels are lowercased and sanitized to alphanumeric + underscore. Truncate labels > 128 chars to 128 to avoid storage blowup.

3) Cost tags: if tenant cannot add cost_center at request time, an ingress-side enrichment will attach a tenant-level cost_center label using the onboarding registry. This must be validated with a sample of 10k requests.

Implementation Steps (Integration Engineer + Tenant)

1) Pre-Work (week -1)
 - Customer Success schedules a 60-minute onboarding sync and assigns an Integrations Engineer (owner).
 - Tenant shares a telemetry sample (ndjson of 24-hour sample or replay harness) or grants access to a staging Kafka topic.

2) Configuration (day 0)
 - Integrations Engineer creates a temporary mapping rule in telemetry-gatekeeper for the tenant.
 - Gateway config: ensure tenant API key is present and routed to the correct ingress-gateway cluster (region matching tenant).
 - Apply retention/policy tags in telemetry-pipeline.

3) Validation Run (days 1-3) — Acceptance Window starts when valid traffic is observed
 - Run replayed traffic or coordinate a controlled production ramp.
 - Run the Validation Tests below hourly and collect artifacts (logs, sample traces, PromQL results).

4) Acceptance Handoff (day 4)
 - If all criteria met: integrator marks telemetry as ACCEPTED and notifies Customer Success.
 - If not met: mark as ACTION_REQUIRED, create a Jira ticket with remediation owner and 72-hour re-test window.

Validation Tests (automated & manual queries)

- Ingestion Latency check (PromQL): 100 * (sum_over_time(redwood.ingest.latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) / sum_over_time(redwood.ingest.requests[5m])) < 60 
- Label completeness check (example SQL against metrics store):
  SELECT count(*) AS total, sum(case when tenant_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_tenant FROM metrics_raw WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '1 hour' AND tenant = '<tenant-marker>';
- Metric coverage report: run the canonical metric families list against observed metric sets and compute percent_present.
- Sample trace integrity: for 1,000 sampled traces, ensure trace_id continuity and presence of "ingress" and "backend" spans in >= 99% of traces.

Rollout & Risk Controls

- Canary Phase: enable telemetry-based billing and SLA reporting for 5% of tenant traffic for 24 hours. Monitor cost attribution and SLO divergence.
- Auto-fallback: if label fidelity drops < 95% or ingestion latency > 120s for 10 consecutive minutes, toggle telemetry-gatekeeper to enrichment-only mode (no normalization writes) and open PagerDuty alert to Integrations On-call.

Ownership and Escalation

- Integration Owner (first-line): Integrations Engineering (owner example: eng-integrations-team). PagerDuty: integrations-oncall@redwood.
- CS Owner: Customer Success Manager listed on the onboarding ticket.
- SRE Owner: observability-oncall for platform-level ingestion issues.

Escalation matrix

1) Integration Owner (2 hours) — fix mapping or config issue.
2) SRE (4 hours) — investigate pipeline/collector outages.
3) Platform Engineering (8 hours) — if root cause is kernel-level ingestion or Kafka/storage issues.

Artifacts to Collect for Acceptance

- Ingestion logs (telemetry-gatekeeper) for the Acceptance Window.
- Sampled traces (ndjson) with a failing example if any spans are missing.
- Prometheus/metrics-store queries showing metric coverage and label completeness.
- Screenshots of dashboards showing token/cost attribution.

QBR Deliverables (post-acceptance)

- Standard QBR deck attachments: metric coverage baseline, fidelity over time, cost attribution mapping, and recommended action items.
- One-time configuration export of the normalization rules (JSON) stored as a config artifact in the tenant onboarding folder.

Appendix: Example Normalization Mappings and Queries

Example mapping chunk (to copy into telemetry-gatekeeper):

  "mappings": [
    {"source_regex": "^app\\.requests\\.(.*)$", "target": "redwood.ingress.requests", "label_transforms": {"ns": "tenant_id"}},
    {"source_regex": "^app\\.latency_ms$", "target": "redwood.request.latency_ms"}
  ]

PromQL example — per-tenant p95 latency:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood.request.latency_ms_bucket{tenant_id=\"<TENANT>\"}[5m])) by (le, tenant_id))

Common Failure Modes and Workarounds

- Missing tenant_id: If tenants cannot emit tenant_id, use ingress API key enrichment and validate via the sample-count method (10k requests).
- High cardinality labels: apply label whitelist at telemetry-gatekeeper and normalize dynamic labels into "label_hash" to avoid metric cardinality explosion.
- Traces missing ingress spans: validate SDK/instrumentation version across services and ensure front-door proxy injects X-TRACE-ID header.

Onboarding Checklist (quick start)

1) Schedule kickoff and identify Integrations Engineer.
2) Tenant provides sample telemetry.
3) Gatekeeper mapping created and tested on staging.
4) Controlled traffic run, run validation tests every hour.
5) Acceptance decision and documentation artifacts uploaded.
